549:
(a) Plans required. No person may sell, offer for sale, lease, rent, begin construction or otherwise begin the physical development of a subdivision or mobile home park where public or community sewage treatment systems are not available or contemplated to be available to serve the proposed development until proposals and plans for the water supply and sewage disposal method to be provided or installed have been submitted to and written approval has been obtained from the county board of health.
(b) Predevelopment review advised. All developers considering subdivision or mobile home park development where public or community sewage treatment systems will not be available are strongly advised to seek a predevelopment review by the county board of health prior to purchasing property and/or making substantial monetary outlays for developmental improvements. Rejection or tentative approval may be obtained at this time by submitting the following information:
(1) A boundary plat including:
a. Vicinity map;
b. A topographic map;
c. A soil map and soil description.
(2) Complete subdivision analysis record on forms provided by the county board of health.
(3) Additional information as required by the county board of health for complete understanding and clarification.
(c) Proposals and plans. Unless previously provided, subdivision or mobile home park proposals shall be submitted on subdivision analysis forms provided by the county board of health. Subdivisions or mobile home park plans shall be drawn to a reasonable scale, with topography depicted by two-foot contour intervals; provided, however, that if ground slope is sufficiently steep for less frequent contour intervals to show the surface configurations, the county board of health may permit the use of lesser contour intervals. Plans shall illustrate the location of all present and proposed wells, watercourses, floodplains, water systems, sewage systems, roads, structures rights-of-way, and easements on the property and within 100 feet outside the perimeter of the property. Subdivision or mobile home park plans shall also include, stormwater drainage systems, elevations of seasonal high water table, location and results of test borings and percolation tests if applicable, lot identification, dimensions, and building lines. The name and registration number of the preparing surveyor or engineer shall also be on the subdivision or mobile home park plans.
(d) Soil evaluation. Data used to develop soil maps and descriptions shall be obtained from reliable sources as set forth in section 32-21(i), soil data acceptability. Where reliable soil information or the services of a soil scientist are not available, percolation tests, soil borings, and such other tests as the county board of health may require shall be conducted.
(e) Limits on use of on-site sewage management systems in subdivision and mobile home parks. Approval of subdivisions and mobile home parks for on-site sewage management systems shall not be granted when:
(1) An available sewer of a public or community sewage treatment system is within 500 feet of the subdivision or mobile home park.
(2) Soil maps, descriptions, and reports compiled by the Soil Conservation Service, U.S. Department of Agriculture, or a soil scientist indicate that soil conditions prohibit safe development with on-site sewage management systems, or the average percolation rate for the subdivision or mobile home park is more than 90 minutes per inch.
(f) Drainage. Where on-site sewage management systems are proposed for use, an adequate surface water drainage system shall be provided for the proper drainage of all surface water. Plans for drainage shall comply with local storm drainage plans and policies in effect in the city and/or county at the time of submission to the county board of health, and approval of drainage plans by the local governing body is a prerequisite to county board of health approval. Additionally, any changes or amendments to approved drainage plans must receive the concurrence of the governing agency, and the county board of health shall be provided with a written approval statement from the governing agency. In the absence of local drainage policies, the county board of health will evaluate drainage plans and render decisions on their acceptability. Plans for internal drainage (subsurface drainage), if used, shall be submitted to the county board of health for consideration as to their acceptability.
(Res. No. 05081997, att. C(290-5-26-.14), 5-8-1997)
550:
(a) Subdivision and mobile home park water supply. A public water supply shall be required if available within 1,000 feet of the proposed subdivision or mobile home park.
(b) Subdivision and mobile home park percolation tests. Where required for planning purposes and determination of the general absorption capacity of soils, the number of percolation tests to be made shall be one per lot, in the area where absorption fields are to be located. Preparatory to construction of on-site sewage management systems, individual lots within the proposed development shall comply with section 32-21 for on-site sewage management systems.
(c) Subdivision and mobile home park test borings. Where required for planning purposes, test borings to determine groundwater elevations and subsurface rock formations shall be made at locations, in numbers and at depths to be determined by the county board of health.
(Res. No. 05081997, att. C(290-5-26-.15), 5-8-1997)
551:
The administration and enforcement of this article shall be in accordance with O.C.G.A. ch. 31-5.
(Res. No. 05081997, att. C(290-5-26-.16), 5-8-1997)
554:
This article shall be known as the rules and regulations for the certification and performance of individual sewage system installers and service workers in the county.
(Ord. No. 061590SS, § 1, 6-15-1990)
555:
Pursuant to the authority vested in the county board of health under 1964 Ga. Laws 1964, pp. 499, 512—518 (Chapter 88-2, Code of Georgia), the county board of health hereby adopts the following rules and regulations for the purposes set forth in section 32-59.
(Ord. No. 061590SS, § 2, 6-15-1990)
556:
The purpose of these rules and regulations is to better safeguard the health of the citizens of the county by requiring individual sewage system installers and service workers to gain a thorough knowledge of health concepts and existing laws, rules and regulations pertaining to installation and maintenance of individual sewage disposal systems and by requiring issuance of a certificate attesting to said knowledge prior to performing the acts ascribed to an individual sewage system installer and service worker as defined in section 32-60.
(Ord. No. 061590SS, § 3, 6-15-1990)
557:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Board means the county board of health, its agents and employees.
Individual sewage disposal system means any water carried sewage disposal system, other than a public sewerage system, which is designed and intended for use as a means of sewage disposal and shall include all piping, tanks, traps, and other related material, equipment, and supplies incident to and normally provided in good practice or which is legally required to be a part of such system. Individual sewage disposal systems used in livestock waste management and other similar operations that are by law the responsibility of agencies other than the state department of human resources or the county boards of health are not included within the scope of this definition.
Individual sewage system installer and service worker means any person who installs, constructs, repairs, makes alterations to, empties, or pumps the contents of an individual sewage disposal system.
Person means any individual, firm, corporation, partnership, association or society.
(Ord. No. 061590SS, § 4, 6-15-1990)
558:
(a) Certification requirements.
(1) After the effective date of the ordinance from which this article is derived, no person shall perform the functions ascribed to an individual sewage system installer and service worker in the county unless he has received a valid certificate from the county board of health or unless he is under the direct supervision of an individual who has received a certificate.
(2) A certification shall be granted to an individual sewage system installer and service worker who displays an acceptable degree of competency on an examination which is compiled and administered by the board. Such examination shall contain questions suitable to the purpose of these rules and regulations and may be administered orally or in writing. The level of competency required on the examination shall be established by the board.
(3) Certificates shall not be transferable from one person to another.
(4) Request for examination shall be in writing. The examination shall be administered within 15 days of the date of the request; provided, however, in the event that the applicant is not successful on the examination, a 30-day waiting period shall be required prior to taking subsequent examinations.
(5) Certificates shall be valid for a period of three years, unless earlier suspended or revoked or until the board requires reexamination as prescribed in subsection (b)(3) of this section.
(b) Certification renewal and reexamination.
(1) An individual sewage system installer and service worker who holds a valid certificate may renew the certificate by making application in writing to the county board of health up to 60 days prior to the three-year expiration date of the certificate then held.
(2) An individual sewage system installer and service worker who holds an expired certificate shall be subject to reexamination by the board prior to reissuance of the certificate in the manner described in subsection (a) of this section.
(3) The board may require reexamination of all individual sewage system installers and service workers holding valid certificates, if in the opinion of the board it is justified due to significant changes in existing laws and rules and regulations. In such instance, the board will notify all certificate holders in writing, and provide a period of six months for reexamination. All certificates issued prior to reexamination as specified in this section shall be invalid at the end of the six-month period designated by the board.
(c) Denial of certificate. When a person has failed to display adequate knowledge and competency on the examination described in subsection (a)(2) of this section, the board shall give written notice of this fact to such person and afford an opportunity for a hearing as specified in section 2.01(a) of Enforcement and Administrative Rules and Procedure for the county.
(d) Intercounty acceptance of certified persons. The county board may accept proof of certification from other county boards of health, provided that their certification is granted on the same or a reasonably similar basis and that written proof of certification is provided by the originating county and signed by the chairman of the board of health or his authorized representative. In the event that the certificate from the originating county is expired, revoked or suspended, the board shall not be required to accept the certificate.
(e) Acceptance of certificates issued under prior rules and regulations. All valid certificates now held by individual sewage system installers and service workers, which were issued under the Rules and Regulations for Certification of Sewage Systems Installers, adopted by the county board of health on October 27, 1989, shall be considered valid until their expiration, revocation or suspension.
(Ord. No. 061590SS, § 5, 6-15-1990)
559:
When in the judgment of the county board of health a certified individual sewage systems installer and service worker violates any provisions of the Rules and Regulations for Individual Sewage System Disposal Systems chapter 270-5-25 (Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. ch. 270-5-25) of the state department of human resources or any subsequent rules and regulations or laws of the county board of health, state department of human resources, or the legislature of the state, which relate to the work performed by individual sewage system installers and service workers or otherwise displays negligence or incompetence, the certificate provided under section 32-61 may be revoked; provided, however, such persons shall be notified of the charges in writing and provided with an opportunity for a hearing as specified in section 2.01(a) of Enforcement and Administrative Rules and Practice and Procedure of the county prior to any such revocation.
(Ord. No. 061590SS, § 6, 6-15-1990)
